goal: Turn Mission Control into a beautiful daily Chief-of-Staff home that recommends the highest-leverage bounded mission, explains the judgment, lets Michael review/edit/approve it and creates a durable agent handoff without embedding browser credentials.
constraints: Recommendation estimates must be explicit and inspectable.
Prefer a safe A0-A2 delegation when available.
Keep all core missions accessible without making them the first visual priority.
No GitHub write token in public browser code.
A3/A4 always stop for explicit human approval.
done_when: One Chief recommendation is visually dominant and evidence-linked.
All core missions remain compactly visible.
Recommendation ranking is deterministic and tested.
Approval creates a durable GitHub mission packet.
UI explicitly states the public Pages runner boundary.
CI and fresh Pages deployment pass.
forbidden: Pretending a static page launched an agent when it only created a handoff

evidence.observation: 18 projects · 7 core missions · 5 delegatable · recommendation PrüfPilot

failures.resolution: Restored exact legacy Mission Control read-only/private-scope/untracked invariants after the harness correctly rejected the first AGENTS rewrite.

uncertainties: Whether the new visual direction feels pleasurable enough remains a human taste judgment after live deployment.
An authenticated agent runner is not yet connected to the public GitHub Pages approval handoff.
next_step: Merge PR #20, refresh GitHub Pages and verify the live v1.0 route.

decision_estimate.rationale: This improves the operating system itself, but current product-proof missions should outrank Mission Control once v1 is shipped.
